best_for: Makers and engineers who design 3D-printable parts as code and want models they can resize by changing one number.

points.title: You write the model
points.text: OpenSCAD is not a click-and-drag modeller. You describe the object in a script and it renders the result, built from solid shapes combined together or 2D outlines extruded into 3D. Great for parametric parts, not for artistic or animated work.

points.title: File formats
points.text: It reads 2D outlines and parameters from DXF files, and reads and writes 3D models as STL and OFF, the usual route to a slicer for 3D printing.

points.title: The stable release dates from 2021
points.text: Version 2021.01 is the latest stable release on every platform listed here. The project also offers release candidates and nightly snapshots with newer features, including the much faster Manifold geometry engine. Snapshots need Windows 10 64-bit or macOS 12 or later.

points.title: Homebrew dropped the Mac cask
points.text: Homebrew disabled the OpenSCAD cask on 2026-09-01 because it fails Apple's Gatekeeper check. The project's page points Mac users to `brew install openscad@snapshot` or MacPorts as alternatives.

points.title: Free under the GPL
points.text: OpenSCAD is free software under the GPL version 2. The Flathub build is verified as published by the OpenSCAD developers, for x64 only.

points.title: Little to downgrade to
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 2 versions and installs for all users on x64. macOS and Linux list only the current release.
